title: Rust/Python route-state consumers bypass the DAO delegation gate on grouped vectors
description: Found reviewing bead 8ck2: the rpl_route_state.json oracle now carries delegations (:12->:11, :13->:15) per spec/05-routing.md 8.7.2, and the C ztest registers them via lichen_rpl_prefix_delegate() so the real fail-closed authorization gate runs (twister 20/20). But the Rust consumer (rust/lichen-rpl/tests/rpl_route_state_vectors.rs) uses process_route_state_diagnostic which per its own comment (rpl_route_state_vectors.rs:440) has no delegation gate, and the Python consumer (python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py evaluate_dao_semantics_for_test_at) passes source_address=None which skips the authorization gate (dao_manager.py:906-912). So the cross-implementation identical-output guarantee for the delegation authorization path currently rests on C alone. Follow-up: wire the oracle's delegations array into the Rust PrefixDelegations (delegate_prefix by public key - note the C delegates by origin address, Rust by pubkey; the oracle may need a key binding field) and the Python dao manager, then assert the grouped vectors through the same gate.
